note_on_method: One of the filter slugs has a lawful data driver in Louisville, and it is the plainest kind: outdoor. The City introduces its whole pickleball list with the sentence "Louisville Parks and Recreation provides several outdoor pickleball courts for all ages.", so every count on the list is an outdoor count and all sixteen published venues qualify. Lights has no driver: the City states no lighting for any venue. Free has none: the City states no price for any court, and its one mention of rentals carries no figure. Indoor has none: the City never uses the word, and the indoor count is left empty rather than written as zero. Public has none anywhere on this site.

slots.why_this_filter:
Every pickleball court in Louisville is outdoor, so this page holds the same sixteen venues and the same sixty-seven courts as the city page. What earns it a URL of its own is that the City drew the line, in one sentence, over the whole set: "Louisville Parks and Recreation provides several outdoor pickleball courts for all ages." That sentence introduces the "Pickleball Court List:", and every one of its seventeen lines sits under it.

The practical reason to read the page is what outdoor means here in the absence of anything else. The City publishes no lighting at any venue, so an outdoor court in Louisville is a daylight court until the City says otherwise, whatever the park hours of 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. suggest. It publishes no surface, so whether a court is asphalt, concrete or acrylic is unknown at all sixteen. It publishes no nets, no price and no parking. The largest sets are Charlie Vettiner's fourteen, then six each at Fern Creek, Hays Kennedy, Wyandotte and Nelson Hornbeck; the smallest are one each at Sun Valley and Riverside Gardens.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the City's pickleball page lists it with a court count under the sentence that calls the set outdoor. Sixteen qualify: Charlie Vettiner, Iroquois, McNeely Lake, Sun Valley, Crescent Hill, Des Pres, Fern Creek, George Rogers Clark, Hays Kennedy, Petersburg, Riverview, Wyandotte, Nelson Hornbeck, Riverside Gardens, Tyler and New Walnut Street.

Two of them need a word. Fern Creek and Riverview qualify on the list line alone, because their park pages do not mention pickleball; the count is the City's, and the silence is recorded on each venue page. What does not qualify is Hounz Lane Park, an outdoor venue on the same sentence with three courts, refused because the Census geocoder places its address in Lyndon city, a separately incorporated small city inside Jefferson County rather than inside Louisville. Nothing is excluded for being indoor, because the City names no indoor court; the indoor figure for Louisville is empty, not zero.

faqs.q: Which outdoor courts in Louisville have lights?
faqs.a: The City does not say, for any venue. Nothing on the pickleball page or any park page mentions lighting, so every venue here is recorded as not stated rather than lit or unlit.
Not stated. The City publishes no price for any court and its pickleball page mentions rentals without a figure, so this site records no fee answer and does not assume a park court is free.

faqs.q: Are there indoor courts in Louisville?
faqs.a: Not on the City's record. Its pickleball page calls the set outdoor and names no indoor court, so the indoor figure is left empty rather than written as zero, and there is no indoor page.
